page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-64 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 512 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Clang software compilation scoring in the top 25%. Image processing tasks also show high efficiency. However, single-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. Large-scale LLM inference represents a notable bottleneck; text generation using a 70B model registers in the bottom 25% at 2.56 tokens per second, reflecting the limitations of CPU-only execution for massive parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-64 offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require expensive specialized hardware or local NVMe drives. It is well-suited for large-scale enterprise databases, memory-cached web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, and moderate data processing pipelines. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for high-speed local scratch space operations or heavy deep learning training.
